main_body: two-story Japanese machiya building with tiled roof
top_band: grey-blue tiled roof slope and ridge cap from rows 1 to 30, plus secondary awning roof slope from rows 41 to 46
evidence: Rows 1-30 show the foreshortened top slope of the main tiled roof with ridge beam and onigawara, followed by a front edge at row 30 and eave shadow at rows 31-32. Below that is the upper plaster facade (rows 33-40), a second foreshortened awning roof slope (rows 41-46) with its own eave shadow (rows 47-50), and the ground floor wooden lattice and recessed noren doorway (rows 51-77).

style.evidence: Richly textured roof tiles with 6+ grey-blue steps, speckled plaster wall with recessed barred windows, detailed wooden lattice (koshi), shaded blue noren curtains, and bamboo-fender (inuyarai) guards at the base. Matches the Beodeul building craft and density.
